dedupe_keys.name: arab union of electricity auptde statistical bulletins 2011 to 2021

description: The Arab Union of Electricity (AUPTDE), founded in Tunis in December 1987 and based in Amman, groups 32 working members from ministries, authorities and utilities of the electricity sector in 19 Arab countries, from Jordan and the United Arab Emirates to Mauritania and Yemen, plus equipment makers and contractors as associate members. On its open data page it publishes its statistical bulletin, one issue per year: the 20th edition for 2011 through the 27th for 2018, and a 28th edition covering 2019 to 2021. It also has committees for distribution, engineering and generation, renewable energy, planning and coordination of the operation of the interconnected Arab electricity networks. Coverage: the member countries' electricity sectors, 2011 to 2021. Format and access: PDF bulletins downloadable from the open data page; free. Licence: not read. Caveats: the bulletins were not opened, so the tables they contain (for example installed capacity, generation, peak load or interconnections) were not checked; the listing shows no issue after 2021, and the site is mainly in Arabic, with an English version of the news. Simulation uses: country-level electricity statistics of Arab states for regional capacity and interconnection studies. Related records: the APEC Energy Database (data-apec-egeda-energy-database) and the CIER statistics (data-cier-latin-america-caribbean-electricity-statistics) are comparable regional electricity statistics.
